The following 
 tables of safe minimum distances from exposed energized electrical equipment 
 shall be maintained in order to provide a safe electrical environment for EEC 
 workers, electrical contractors and the general public.

Each table applies to 
 specific circumstances corresponding to equipment design and work procedures 
 and shall be interpreted by authorized EEHC staff accordingly, as outlined in 
 the EEC Electrical Safety Rules.

This document was amended according to "Official 
 Journal" issue no. 26 at 27 June 1991 regard to Law no. 204 for 1991 ''Rights 
 of Way's Law''. so 
 table no. 6 was amended at 16 Oct 2005.

Exposed Energized Electrical Equipment is defined as any electrical 
 apparatus or conductor and attached hardware that is not protected by a cover, 
 jacket or barrier and is dynamically charged.

This equipment shall be considered energized until isolation has been 
 verified and approved earthing procedures have been completed.

Introduction
The following 
 tables of safe minimum distances from exposed energized electrical equipment 
 shall be maintained in order to provide a safe electrical environment for EEC 
 workers, electrical contractors and the general public.
Each table applies to 
 specific circumstances corresponding to equipment design and work procedures 
 and shall be interpreted by authorized EEHC staff accordingly, as outlined in 
 the EEC Electrical Safety Rules.
This document was amended according to "Official 
 Journal" issue no. 26 at 27 June 1991 regard to Law no. 204 for 1991 ''Rights 
 of Way's Law''. so 
 table no. 6 was amended at 16 Oct 2005.
Definition
Exposed Energized Electrical Equipment is defined as any electrical 
 apparatus or conductor and attached hardware that is not protected by a cover, 
 jacket or barrier and is dynamically charged.
This equipment shall be considered energized until isolation has been 
 verified and approved earthing procedures have been completed.
